competition.headline: University of Montana funds 125-device Brick phone-blocking program
competition.summary: UM's Curry Health Center bought 125 Brick NFC-blocking devices for a 'Be Here with Brick' campus program, funded by a $6,800 campus grant and including a semester loan program for students. A direct institutional win for a punitive/physical-blocking competitor in the exact higher-ed wellness space NOMO's rewards model targets.

industry.headline: Meta's $17.1B teen social media settlement finalized with 51-state AG coalition
industry.summary: A bipartisan coalition of 51 attorneys general secured a landmark settlement forcing Meta to adopt court-mandated defaults like time limits and nighttime blackouts. Locks in platform-side behavior change that validates NOMO's reward-for-reduced-screen-time thesis and primes schools/states to favor third-party tools that reinforce it.

industry.headline: UK confirms under-16 social media ban with hard age checks, effective March 2027
industry.summary: The UK government is preparing to mandate passport/ID-level age verification for under-16 social media access, with the ban taking effect by March 2027; restrictions for 16-17 year-olds on infinite scroll/algorithmic content remain undated. Gives NOMO's UK pilot a concrete regulatory horizon and leaves room for CEO Leonardo's ongoing policy engagement to shape scope.

industry.headline: Canada moves toward Australia-style under-16 social media ban
industry.summary: Ottawa's proposed under-16 ban has drawn a generally warm response, though experts flag unclear accountability mechanisms for platforms; Snap's parent company has separately signaled openness to teen time restrictions. A third major English-speaking market joins the global policy wave NOMO already tracks in US/UK/AU.

industry.headline: Europe pushes toward 15-year social media age limit with one-hour daily cap for 13-15s
industry.summary: Emerging EU framework would cap teen social media use at one hour/day with overnight lockouts and no personal accounts for 13-15 year-olds. A prescriptive regulatory template that directly validates NOMO's core mechanic and could inform UK/US policy conversations.

industry.headline: California and Australia compared as blueprints for state-level youth social media crackdowns
industry.summary: California's new law targets addictive features (algorithms, infinite scroll, autoplay) and requires feature-free accounts for under-16s; experts warn minor-only restrictions face an 'uphill battle' given parent/peer modeling. Directly relevant cross-market read for NOMO's US GTM-now push and AU exploratory signal, reinforcing demand for school/family-level behavioral alternatives.

new_candidates.name: Dayo (Dayo Deals)
new_candidates.why_fits: Dayo pays teens cash for staying under agreed screen-time limits and already has Starbucks, Adidas, and Amazon as reward brands — the closest direct competitor to NOMO's Moments-for-offline-time model, overlapping with the same brand-reward pool NOMO taps via Nike/Vans.

new_candidates.name: Linewize EdTech Manager (Qoria)
new_candidates.why_fits: Linewize's newly launched district-wide Screen Time reporting feature (a Tech & Learning award winner) puts Qoria in direct competition for the same K-12 school procurement conversations NOMO needs, offering districts a monitoring-only alternative to a reward-based model.

new_candidates.name: The Commons
new_candidates.why_fits: The Commons is being adopted by districts (e.g., WSCUHSD/Analy High for 2026-27) as a geofenced app-blocker for the school day — a direct rival for the same 6-12 Education contracts NOMO pursues, competing on block-first rather than reward-first positioning.

new_candidates.name: Yondr
new_candidates.why_fits: Yondr's phone pouches now anchor a bell-to-bell policy at the largest NY State district to adopt one (Lackawanna), showing physical-blocking vendors winning the same district contracts NOMO's reward model competes for.

new_candidates.name: Rogers Screen Break
new_candidates.why_fits: Rogers built its own $50M, five-year national youth screen-balance program rather than seeking a distribution partner, showing telcos may choose to own this space directly instead of white-labeling a rewards layer — worth tracking as a template competitor even though Canada is exploratory-signal-only region for NOMO.

new_candidates.name: Lock&Stock
new_candidates.why_fits: Lock&Stock rewards students with 'keys' for offline time, redeemable for brand discounts and scholarships, and has scaled its SecureMyScholarship model to 1,000+ universities — a close mechanical twin to NOMO's Moments system targeting the college market.

new_candidates.name: TAP: Tech Activity Pact
new_candidates.why_fits: TAP lets teens negotiate screen-time 'pacts' with parents and earn bonus rewards for follow-through via streaks — mechanically the closest new entrant to NOMO's own streaks/leaderboard/social-accountability design.

new_candidates.name: Dallas Teen All-Access Pass (Dallas Park and Recreation Department)
new_candidates.why_fits: Dallas's free Teen All-Access Pass bundles zoo, arboretum, and recreation-venue access for 13-17 year-olds — comparable experiential-pass inventory to NOMO's Fever (concerts & museums) and GetYourGuide partnerships, and realistic to approach since it's a municipal program rather than a single paid brand.

new_candidates.name: TeenTix
new_candidates.why_fits: TeenTix's $5 teen pass covering movies, music, theatre, dance and visual art extends NOMO's Odeon/Ingresso-style entertainment rewards into an arts/theatre category it doesn't yet cover.

new_candidates.name: Go City
new_candidates.why_fits: Go City's bundled attraction/museum passes across 28 cities on 4 continents would broaden NOMO's Fever/GetYourGuide-style experience rewards into a scalable, multi-city format NOMO's current lineup lacks.

new_candidates.name: Sonic Drive-In
new_candidates.why_fits: Sonic's new loyalty program offering free fries/tots/drinks for sign-up gives NOMO cheap, high-frequency, teen-friendly reward inventory in a food & drink category where it currently has zero partners.

new_candidates.name: Planet Fitness Teen Summer Pass
new_candidates.why_fits: Planet Fitness's free teen gym pass across 2,400+ locations is a nationally scalable, low-cost reward comparable in structure to NOMO's existing Vans/Nike/Down Dog lifestyle rewards, adding physical fitness-facility access NOMO doesn't yet have.

new_candidates.name: Topgolf (via Topgolf Media Networks)
new_candidates.why_fits: Topgolf's new Media Networks division is actively building sponsorship/licensing deals and already runs teen leadership programming at 25+ venues, making it a plausible experience-reward partner alongside NOMO's GetYourGuide/Odeon-style outings.

new_candidates.name: Young Life
new_candidates.why_fits: Young Life's RELATE 2026 study found youth 'digitally saturated yet their relational circles are shrinking' — a direct thesis match for NOMO's offline-rewards model, and a genuine first mover for the currently-empty Faith-based & Youth Orgs GTM vertical.

new_candidates.name: City of Dallas Parks & Recreation (Teen All Access Pass)
new_candidates.why_fits: Dallas Parks & Rec already runs the municipal infrastructure (venue partnerships, teen sign-up flow) behind its free Teen All-Access Pass, making it a ready-built Municipalities-vertical implementation partner for NOMO, which currently has zero GTM partners.

new_candidates.name: Massachusetts Dept. of Elementary & Secondary Education (Phone-Free Schools Grant)
new_candidates.why_fits: Massachusetts has already put $1M+ in phone-free school grants behind 77 districts (following a $1.3M pilot), giving NOMO a concrete state funding mechanism to plug into as the reward/accountability layer behind phone-free policy — directly filling NOMO's empty Municipalities & States GTM lineup.

new_candidates.name: State Attorneys General Meta Settlement Fund (50-state coalition)
new_candidates.why_fits: The 51-AG coalition's up-to-$17.1B Meta settlement is earmarked for youth mental-health and digital-wellbeing programs — a large, newly available funding pool states could direct toward implementation partners like NOMO, a genuine first entrant into NOMO's currently empty state/municipal GTM channel.

new_candidates.name: Digital Schools Awards x Ygam
new_candidates.why_fits: This new England/Scotland schools-network partnership delivering digital wellbeing training for 2026-27 is exactly the kind of school distribution channel NOMO's UK pilot needs, especially given CEO Leonardo's active UK policy engagement.

new_candidates.name: California AB 3216 phone-free districts wave (e.g., Central Unified SD, Davis Joint USD)
new_candidates.why_fits: California's Phone-Free Schools Act is forcing districts like Central Unified and Davis Joint USD to build 2026-27 implementation plans right now — a concrete, time-bound procurement window for NOMO's 6-12 Education vertical in its highest-weighted US market.

new_candidates.name: LeagueApps
new_candidates.why_fits: LeagueApps just became Red Bull New York's official youth-soccer registration partner, reaching 50,000+ players and families — exactly the coach/parent-touchpoint distribution NOMO needs to fill its empty Youth Sports GTM vertical without signing leagues one by one.

new_candidates.name: UnitedHealthcare
new_candidates.why_fits: UnitedHealthcare just expanded child/family behavioral coaching to roughly 13 million eligible members, showing insurer appetite for scaled teen behavioral-health benefits — an opening for NOMO to slot in as a complementary screen-time/wellness benefit in a new Insurance distribution vertical.

With no GTM partners currently signed, an integration or co-marketing deal with a platform already embedded in rosters/communications would be a strong distribution shortcut.
